Company name: SAP Labs
Location for Internship: Bangalore
Eligibility: 7+ CGPA
Day 1- Online Test
September 1, 2017
Test Duration: 90 mins.
Platform: mettl.com
This test consisted 6 sections out of which 4 were MCQ based and remaining 2 were based on 
actual coding. The detailed distribution was as follows:
MCQs were easy. I was able to solve all of the MCQs and was sure about it. Coding 1 section 
consisted of 2 questions (debugging). For each question one problem statement and a piece of 
code was given. We had to rectify all of its logical and syntactical errors. I was able to solve ﬁrst 
one completely and second one partially. Partially in a sense, I removed all syntax errors and was 
able to run program but was not able to produce complete output.
In coding 2 section, 2 programming questions were there. As I attempted this section at last, I 
almost ran out of time. I solved only one question.
This was around 2 in afternoon. In evening results were announced and only 9 candidates were 
shortlisted for interviews. 6 from Comps and 3 from IT.
Day 2- Interviews
September 2, 2017
We gathered in TPO seminar hall at 9.00 a.m. Be very punctual as when I reached TPO at 9, 
people from company were already there and one of them was interacting with students. After their 
presentation they collected our resume and then they started calling our names for interview.
There were 3 rounds of interview, each with elimination. 
Interview 1: Technical
9 Candidates
 
Before starting we shook hands and he offered me to sit. From my resume he directly jumped on 
my project section and asked about them. What role did I play. I spoke to him regarding that and 
mentioned one project I was comfortable talking with. Around half an hour we discussed about the 
project. When you say you know your project, you seriously need to know everything about it. 
Though we discussed about what all technologies I have used in the project ( e.g. HTML, CSS, 
PHP and MySQL) but his main focus was on database. Discussion started with exact description of 
project and its functionalities. He then asked me to draw ER diagram of my database tables. I was

not properly mentioning every ﬁeld in the table, so he told me that he wants me to write every ﬁeld 
also. But yeah, I was prepared as I had gone through my project once before interview. Then he 
asked me about relationships, different keys(primary, candidate, super, foreign etc) and how I was 
executing different functions in php. So I had to write php code for whatever he was asking. He 
asked me how I was using SESSION to keep track of user. After knowing quite a bit about my 
project, he started giving me database design scenarios where I had to modify my table design and 
give him solution (Be prepared to write a lot of queries). Then he gave me some question 
regarding SQL Joins and asked about normalisation, transactions and ACID properties. He asked 
whether I had my laptop to show him the working project, I replied negatively. Apart from database 
discussion ( which was like half of my interview), he asked me what all computer science related 
subjects we had till now.  He then asked me about operating systems. In that he asked about role 
of operations system, process and virtual memory. I said what I knew and told him that my 
knowledge of this subject is very limited as this subject is still to be taught. He said okay and went 
on asking different topics. He asked me about CSS and what I liked about it. I told him about 
importance of front-end. As I   had mentioned in my resume about winning medals on Hackerrank, 
he asked me what all type of question did I solve. And told me to say few questions that I recently 
have solved on Hackerrank. He asked me to write a proper code for a question of linked list. The 
question was very easy. It was deleting a node from a linked list given a value. I solved it and 
explained to him. It is very important to tell him what you are doing or how you are planning to 
solve the problem. He also asked about arrays and linked list. Comparing each ones 
properties( access, search, delete etc). He asked about stack and queues and asked for real life 
examples. We then discussed about stack overﬂow and how will it happen. I gave an example of a 
recursive function. The interviewer was an experienced person and was very kind and supportive. 
It was a comfortable conversation that’s why I cannot recall every question here. These are some I 
remembered.
At the end of interview he asked me if I had any question. I asked some. He answered this brieﬂy 
about 3-4 minutes and then again we shook hands and I left.
After ﬁrst interview 4 candidates were eliminated. Rest 5 were called for next interview.
Interview 2: Technical
5 Candidates
This interview started with tell me about yourself. He told me that he will start with a Maths 
question. He asked to ﬁnd sum of series of 
!
 + ……
I said it is an inﬁnite GP and we can solve it directly using formula. He told me not to use formula. I 
then gave him easy solution without formula. He then told me to always think simple. He also 
started with database designing problem for students etc. For a particular solution of mine we 
discussed for a long time why it was not an efﬁcient solution. He then gave me hint to ﬁnd a better 
one. Again we discussed on that also. He moved to C++ and asked about friend functions. He 
asked about runtime and compile time polymorphism and told me to write a code for it (Go through 
concept of virtual functions properly). He asked me about Java saying why Java is platform 
independent. Discussion involved jdk, jre and jvm and importance and role of jvm. He asked about 
properties of OOP, access speciﬁer and their difference. Other questions were upon Abstract 
classes, Interfaces, What are Exceptions and how to handle them  (write code) and some question 
related to inheritance, singleton and factory patterns. He asked what my favourite subject was. I 
said Data Structures. He asked lots of questions. He covered topics like Array, Linked List, Stacks, 
Queues and Binary trees. He then asked me to write a proper code to ﬁnd second maximum in a 
list of numbers (What can be easier than this!). I wrote and explained to him. He then asked me to 
show it using an example. Before leaving, he asked if I had some questions. I asked some and he 
gave short answer to that. We shook hands and I left.

After second round only one candidate was eliminated.
Interview 3: HR
4 Candidates
This was short and sweet interview. Every time, interviewer was asking me to keep going on, even 
when I was ﬁnished answering. He started with my project and what it was like. He asked me to tell 
him about myself apart from things I had mentioned in my resume. He asked about my Design 
Head responsibility and we brieﬂy discussed that. He questioned about what I seek in life apart 
from getting a job. He then asked me to elaborate my answer. He gave me a puzzle to solve (SAP 
has a tendency to ask puzzles). I was able to solve it. He then told me he didn’t get what I did. I 
again explained to him. He asked if we had hosted our website. I replied negatively. He then asked 
how will I sell my website to an investor with the fact that there are many better websites available 
for the same purpose. He then asked me if I had some idea about monetisation and collaboration 
with distributors.
During interview he asked the meaning of my name. Discussion involved my hobbies and why 
didn’t I choose them as my career. 
Apart from knowing myself, he asked general questions such as why SAP. I replied with reference 
to their presentation I attended in morning. He asked if I am willing to move to Bangalore and will I 
be able to manage things there. He asked if I knew what stipend and proﬁle they were offering. Will 
I take PPO if offered by company in future. For what period of internship I will be available and 
when. 
He asked me if I wanted to ask some question to him. I denied. Again we spoke for few minutes 
and he told me that I have been selected for internship.
I waited for my friends. In evening around 6, results were announced.
All 4 were selected.
  
Summary:
1 online round
2 technical interviews
1 HR interview
For technical interview, focus on:
1.
Basic concepts in programming
2.
Datastructure and algorithms
3.
Operating system
4.
DBMS and Sql (most important)
5.
OOP and JAVA (important)
6.
Puzzles
Go through the projects you are mentioning in resume. Your interview is somehow dependent on 
your resume so put only those things which you know you can answer. 
Good Luck!
